note_on_method: This is a state page, so most of it is a claim about coverage rather than about a court. Where it describes a place, the source is that operator's own publication - the City of Irvine's pickleball page, court regulations page and park pages, the City of Huntington Beach's Park Amenities page, the City of Long Beach's pickleball page and park directory. Where it describes what is missing, it names the venue or the city and says why it is not here, because 'not listed' and 'does not exist' are different things and a reader deserves to know which one they are reading. Statements about the cities that have not been read - Los Angeles, Anaheim, Santa Ana, Pasadena and the rest - are statements about a reading list on one day, not about their courts. This page exists because Long Beach was published on 7 September 2026, giving California three verified cities. Nobody working on this has played on any court in California.

slots.coverage:
California has fifty-eight counties. This page covers three cities in two of them.

Fifteen venues, 79 courts, three municipal operators, all read on 7 September 2026. Orange County holds seven of the venues and 31 of the courts, in two cities: Irvine, three venues and eighteen courts, and Huntington Beach, four venues and thirteen. Los Angeles County holds eight venues and 48 courts, all inside Long Beach. Every venue is run by a city parks department - the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center is managed for the City of Long Beach under contract by BTG Tennis & Pickleball, and it sits in the City's own park directory - and not one private club, gated-community court, school gym or commercial facility appears. That is a statement about who writes court counts down rather than about where pickleball in California is played.

A venue publishes when its operator states a court count and an address that resolves inside the city, a city when three or more of its venues do, and a state when three of its cities do. Long Beach, published on 7 September 2026, was California's third.

The three cities arrived by three different kinds of document, and the differences decide what each can be said to have. Irvine states every count twice - once in a sentence on its pickleball page, "eight lit pickleball courts located at Mike Ward Community Park, six lit pickleball courts located at Portola Springs Community Park, four lit pickleball courts located at Heritage Park", and once in each park's own amenity list as "8 Lighted Pickleball Courts" and so on - and the three venues where the two records agree publish, with lighting, hours of 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily and a reservation price all in the City's words. Huntington Beach states everything it states in four lines under one heading on its Park Amenities page, "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)", each line a name, an address and a count - "Edison Park - 21377 Magnolia St. - 4 Courts" - and nothing else: no hours, no price, no surface. Long Beach gives each park one line under "Pickleball Courts at Park Locations:" with the address in brackets and a count that says whether the courts are dedicated or striped onto something else - "DeForest Park (6255 DeForest Ave.) - 8 dedicated courts.", "Veterans Park (101 E. 28th St.) - Hybrid location: 8 pickleball courts on 1 tennis court and 4 dedicated pickleball courts." - and where a line carries two figures the published count is the City's own sum. Twenty-three of Long Beach's 48 are dedicated on those lines; the City's headline sentence says "Currently there are 24 dedicated pickleball courts in Long Beach", and the list is published rather than the total, because the two do not agree.

What is stated nowhere is as much a part of the record as what is stated. No operator in the three cities calls any court indoor or outdoor, so the indoor and outdoor breakdowns are empty for all fifteen venues and no California city has an indoor or an outdoor page. No operator writes the word free: Irvine prices four reservable courts and calls the other fourteen first come, first served; Huntington Beach prices reserved tennis courts at $9 an hour and never prices a pickleball court; Long Beach calls its park courts first come, first served and prices its tennis centre. First come, first served is a play format, not a price, so no California venue is recorded as free. No operator names a surface.

Four venues on the three Cities' own pages are absent, and they are named rather than dropped. Los Olivos Community Park in Irvine is "two lit pickleball courts" on the City's pickleball page and its regulations page and "3 Lighted Pickleball Courts" on the park's own page, and a count the operator states two ways cannot publish. The Billie Jean King Tennis Center in Long Beach is the same shape: "four shared-use pickleball courts" on the City's pickleball page, "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted" on the centre's own. Somerset Park has a stated count, "Dual striping 8 pickleball on 2 tennis courts", and an address, "1500 E. Carson", that the Census geocoder places in the neighbouring city of Carson, postcode 90745, so it cannot sit on a Long Beach page. Whaley Park is "Dual-striped pickleball and volleyball court" with no number. Huntington Beach refused nothing; its four lines are its four venues.

Beyond the three, the rest of California has not been read, and that is a statement about a reading list rather than about courts. Long Beach's own page summarises its neighbours - Los Angeles, Cerritos, Torrance, Seal Beach, Anaheim, Tustin and Lakewood among them - and none of that summary is used, because a city's courts publish from that city's own pages. Anaheim, Santa Ana, Newport Beach and Costa Mesa in Orange County, and Los Angeles, Pasadena, Torrance and Santa Monica in Los Angeles County, have no page here because nobody has read them against a named source, not because they were read and failed.
slots.seasonality:
None of the three California operators states a season, a rain policy, a heat policy or a summer closure, and this page will not supply one from memory. What they state falls into three kinds: hours that run to a clock, hours that run to the sun, and lights.

Irvine's hours run to a clock. All three parks are "6 a.m.-10 p.m., Daily" on their own pages, and every one of the eighteen courts is lit in the City's own word, so the window is sixteen hours long and does not shrink in December. The City's reservation windows sit inside it - "between the hours of 7 a.m. to noon, and 4 to 10 p.m." for Courts #3 and #4 at Mike Ward and Courts #5 and #6 at Portola Springs - and those two blocks are the nearest thing Irvine publishes to a statement of when its courts are wanted. The Irvine Team Pickleball league is "a 7-week Round Robin and a 3-week single-elimination playoffs" with no month printed beside it.

Huntington Beach's hours run to the sun, because the City states no hours at all and one parenthesis instead: "(NO LIGHTING)". Thirteen courts in four parks, none usable after dark, so a weekday evening game is possible in June and not in December, and the City has said so without printing an opening time. The trap is the City's tennis page, which prints "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" for lighted tennis courts at Edison Community Park and Marina Park - the same addresses as two of the pickleball venues - and that closing time belongs to tennis courts, which these are not. The same tennis page carries the one weather word in the three cities' pickleball record: OC Racquet Sports' number, "(760) 902-0686 - (also the rain hotline)", for clinics the City describes as serving "your tennis or pickleball goals". Which courts those clinics use, and what the hotline says about a park court on a wet morning, is not stated.

Long Beach runs both ways. DeForest Park's page reads "Park Hours: Dawn to Dusk", the one park in the city with stated hours for the park itself, and they move with the sun. The El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center runs to a clock - "Monday through Friday: 7am- 9:30pm Saturday, & Sunday: 7am - 8pm" - and its pickleball inside that is scheduled: drop-in "on Tuesday and Thursday mornings from 8 to 11 am, and Friday evenings from 6 to 9pm" as the page stood when read, with "NO LIGHT FEES" and "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted". Silverado Park and El Dorado Park West print hours that move with the school calendar - "Regular School (LBUSD) Year Hours", "Afterschool Programming (during school year)" - but those govern a community centre and its programmes, not a court, and are not carried across. The other Long Beach parks state no hours and no lighting either way.

Put the three together and the evening picture in verified California is this: four venues stated lit, 26 courts - Mike Ward, Portola Springs and Heritage in Irvine, and the El Dorado tennis centre in Long Beach; four venues stated unlit, thirteen courts, all in Huntington Beach; and seven venues, forty courts, all Long Beach parks, where the City says nothing either way. El Dorado Park West's page says the park has "night-lighted basketball and multi-use courts", and its three pickleball courts are "on a shared sports court"; whether the one is the other is not something the City says, so the venue stays in the unknown column.

The indoor answer is shorter still. No operator in the three cities uses the word indoor or outdoor about a pickleball court, so the verified indoor count for California is not zero but unstated, and no city here has an indoor page. A reader looking for a roof in a California winter will not find one on these pages, and will not find a statement that there is none.
slots.notable:
Veterans Park in Long Beach is the largest verified pickleball venue in California on these pages, at twelve courts, and the twelve is the City's own arithmetic: "Hybrid location: 8 pickleball courts on 1 tennis court and 4 dedicated pickleball courts." Eight of the twelve are lines on a single tennis court, and the City's rule for every park court applies - "first-come, first-served and court signage regarding shared use must be observed" - so the number a player finds depends on who arrived first and what the sign says. Four are pickleball courts whatever is happening beside them. The park's own page, which lists two tennis courts, a lighted softball field and a community centre on 14.3 acres, does not mention pickleball at all.

Four venues hold eight, and they are eight in four different ways. DeForest Park's are "8 dedicated courts", the largest dedicated set in the state on these pages, on the fifteen City-owned acres of a 49.6-acre site whose remaining acres are the DeForest Wetlands and nature trail, with hours of "Dawn to Dusk". Mike Ward Community Park's are "eight lit pickleball courts", open until 10 p.m. daily, two of them - Courts #3 and #4 - reservable at "Resident Rate: $17/hr" and "Non-Resident Rate: $19/hr". Marina Vista Park's are "4 dedicated pickleball courts and 4 dual-striped courts for either tennis or pickleball", at a park the City's pickleball page locates only by cross streets, "Colorado St. & Santiago", and whose own page gives "5355 Eliot St." The El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center's are "eight shared-use pickleball courts", "Fully Lighted", and priced: "$5 per person for drop-in play (up to three hours), while private pickleball court reservations are $10 per court per hour". It is the one venue in Long Beach with a price, a lighting answer and clock hours, and it shares its address, 2800 Studebaker Road, with El Dorado Park West's three park courts, which publish as a separate venue.

Portola Springs Community Park is the home of the one league any California operator publishes, Irvine Team Pickleball: "Eight teams face off in a 7-week Round Robin and a 3-week single-elimination playoffs", "a self-rated level 3.5 league", "$490 per team per season", on six lit courts of which Courts #5 and #6 are reservable. Heritage Community Park has four lit courts in the largest of the Irvine parks at approximately 36.5 acres, beside "12 Lighted Tennis Courts", and it is the one Irvine venue with no reservable court; the City is "currently developing a master plan" for it.

Junipero Beach is notable for where it is and what it was: "2 dedicated pickleball courts on repurposed half basketball court", at 2100 E. Ocean Blvd, with no park page in the City's directory, so the one line is the whole record. Two courts is a game, not a rotation.

Huntington Beach's notable fact is a heading rather than a venue. "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)" answers the lighting question for Boardwalk, Edison, Marina and Worthy at once, in the negative, and it is why those thirteen courts publish as unlit rather than as unknown, while Long Beach's forty park courts, about which the City says nothing, do not. Boardwalk Park's "1 Court" is one game at a time and daylight only.

The most notable California venue that is not published is the Billie Jean King Tennis Center in Long Beach, "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted" on its own page, with "NO LIGHT FEES" and hours to 9:30 p.m. on weekdays, and "four shared-use pickleball courts" on the City's pickleball page. It fails on the count alone. Somerset Park's "Dual striping 8 pickleball on 2 tennis courts" is the one refused count the City states only one way, and it fails on a boundary: the Census places "1500 E. Carson" in Carson. Los Olivos Community Park in Irvine, two courts on two City pages and three on a third, has a resolving address and lit courts and fails on the one fact a court page cannot do without.
slots.growth:
Nothing in California is published as a court count that changed, and this page will not describe growth on its own authority. What the three Cities print is one sentence that uses the word, two notices of intent, a set of reservation and schedule changes written in the present tense, and three counts that differ from the ones this site had imported.

The sentence is Long Beach's: "Pickleball continues to be a growing sport in Long Beach. Staff has worked hard with the Long Beach Pickleball Advisory Group to identify locations to enjoy this exciting activity." It is followed by the "24 dedicated pickleball courts" total that the City's own list does not reach, which is the ordinary shape of a record written faster than it is reconciled. The list itself shows how the courts were found: "2 dedicated pickleball courts on repurposed half basketball court" at Junipero Beach, "8 pickleball courts on 1 tennis court" at Veterans, "3 pickleball courts on a shared sports court" at El Dorado Park West. Twenty-five of the City's 48 courts are on ground that was something else first, and the 23 dedicated courts are the other half. The City's tennis centre is written the same way: drop-in pickleball on two mornings and a Friday evening now, and "Future offerings will expand drop-in play on every weekday morning from 8 to 11 am" with reservations "from 11 am to 4 pm Monday thru Friday on eight courts". The park rule is "NO reservations at this time", and "at this time" is the City's phrase, not this page's.

The notices of intent are Irvine's. "The City is evaluating building pickleball courts at the Great Park", on the pickleball page, and "The City of Irvine is currently developing a master plan for Heritage Community Park", on that park's page. Neither carries a count, a date or a drawing, and neither adds anything to the eighteen. Irvine's reservation system is written as new - "Pickleball court reservations are now available at Portola Springs Community Park (Courts #5 and #6) and Mike Ward Community Park (Courts #3 and #4)" - and it prices four of the eighteen courts. The City's own totals for its inventory - "12 public pickleball courts" on the regulations page, twenty by the pickleball page's per-park sentence, and ten, nine or eight hybrid courts depending on which sentence is read - are the clearest sign on these pages of an inventory moving faster than the pages that describe it.

Huntington Beach prints nothing about change at all. Its four lines carry no date, its tennis page prices a tennis court, and the one thing it states about its pickleball courts beyond a count and an address is that they have no lights.

The three counts that changed are this site's, not the Cities'. Heritage Community Park was imported at two courts and the City states four; Veterans Park was imported at eight and the City's line sums to twelve; Marina Vista Park was imported at four and the City's line sums to eight. Each is flagged for a re-read at the next cadence, and each is more likely a better record than a construction notice, because no City says a court was built. The El Dorado centre's drop-in fee was imported at $10 and the City says $5 per person.

What Long Beach writes about its neighbours is the nearest thing to a regional statement on these pages, and it is quoted as what Long Beach writes and not used as a source: "LA City Parks has four dedicated, lighted pickleball courts and 34 shared-use courts", with eight more described as under development. Los Angeles will publish from its own pages or not at all.

What would change this page most is a record rather than a court. Los Olivos publishes the day Irvine's three pages agree; the Billie Jean King centre the day Long Beach's two do; Somerset Park the day its address resolves inside Long Beach; Whaley Park the day the City writes a number. Every quoted sentence above is snapshotted into the repository that builds this page and re-asserted on every build, so if Long Beach reconciles its 24 with its 23, Irvine prints a count for the Great Park, or Huntington Beach moves a park out from under its heading, the build fails and someone reads the page again.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in California?
faqs.a: Nobody can tell you honestly, and this page will not pretend to. What has been checked is 79 courts across fifteen venues in three cities - Long Beach with 48, Irvine with 18, Huntington Beach with 13 - each with a named source and a date. The three Cities' own pages name four more venues that fail on a count the City states two ways, an address the Census places in Carson, or no number at all.

Because three is how many have been read against an operator page that states a count and an address for three or more venues. Irvine, Huntington Beach and Long Beach were all read on 7 September 2026. Los Angeles, Anaheim, Santa Ana, Pasadena, Torrance, Santa Monica and the rest of the state have not been read at all, which says nothing about their courts; Long Beach's one-sentence summaries of its neighbours are not used as a source for them.

Four venues, 26 courts. Mike Ward, Portola Springs and Heritage in Irvine are "lit" on the City's pickleball page and "Lighted" in each park's amenity list, eighteen courts open until 10 p.m. daily. The El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center in Long Beach is "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted". All four Huntington Beach parks are stated unlit under one heading. Seven Long Beach parks, forty courts, carry no lighting answer, which means nobody has said, not that the courts are dark.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in California?
faqs.a: No verified venue in California is recorded as free, because no operator writes the word. Irvine prices four reservable courts at $17 an hour for residents and $19 for non-residents and states no price for the other fourteen. Long Beach calls its park courts first come, first served, which is a play format, and prices its tennis centre at $5 per person for drop-in play and $10 per court per hour to reserve. Huntington Beach prices tennis courts and says nothing about pickleball.

faqs.q: Where can I play indoors in California?
faqs.a: Nowhere on these pages, and not because there is nowhere. None of the three Cities uses the word indoor or outdoor about any pickleball court, so all fifteen venues carry an empty indoor and outdoor breakdown and no California city has an indoor page. That is a gap in what the operators write, recorded as a gap rather than filled in from a photograph or a map.

faqs.q: What is the biggest pickleball site in California?
faqs.a: Veterans Park in Long Beach, at twelve courts - "8 pickleball courts on 1 tennis court and 4 dedicated pickleball courts" in the City's words, so eight of them are shared with tennis. Four venues follow at eight: DeForest Park's eight dedicated courts, Mike Ward Community Park's eight lit courts in Irvine, Marina Vista Park's four dedicated and four dual-striped, and the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center's eight lit shared-use courts.

faqs.q: Can I book a court anywhere in California?
faqs.a: At two Irvine parks and one Long Beach tennis centre. Courts #3 and #4 at Mike Ward and Courts #5 and #6 at Portola Springs are booked online, residents five days ahead and non-residents three, in one- or two-hour blocks between 7 a.m. and noon and 4 and 10 p.m. The El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center takes private pickleball reservations at $10 per court per hour. Long Beach's park courts are "NO reservations at this time", and Huntington Beach publishes no booking route for pickleball.

faqs.q: Why are Los Olivos, Somerset Park, the Billie Jean King Tennis Center and Whaley Park not listed?
faqs.a: Three different reasons. Los Olivos in Irvine and the Billie Jean King centre in Long Beach each carry two City counts - two courts and three, four courts and eight - and a count the operator states two ways cannot publish. Somerset Park's stated eight courts sit at "1500 E. Carson", which the Census geocoder places in the city of Carson rather than Long Beach. Whaley Park's line, "Dual-striped pickleball and volleyball court", has no number in it.

All three Cities' pages were read on 7 September 2026. They are static web pages that change without notice, so each is snapshotted into the repository that builds these pages and every quoted sentence is re-asserted on every build. If Irvine's three Los Olivos figures agree, Long Beach reconciles its 24 dedicated courts with the 23 on its list, or Huntington Beach moves a park out from under its no-lighting heading, the build fails and the page is read again.

sources.evidence: County resolved per venue for all fifteen published California venues: the three Irvine addresses and the four Huntington Beach addresses in Orange County (FIPS 06059), inside the incorporated places "Irvine city" and "Huntington Beach city"; the eight Long Beach addresses in Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037), inside "Long Beach city", six through the Census address file and two - "5355 Eliot St." and "2800 Studebaker Road" - through OpenStreetMap because the Census added a compass direction the City does not write. For Portola Springs the Census returns 92618 where the City's page prints 92620, and the Census value is published. "1500 E. Carson", the address the City of Long Beach publishes for Somerset Park, is placed by the Census in "Carson city", postcode 90745. Snapshots: data/sources/irvine-county-census.json, data/sources/huntington-beach-county-census.json, data/sources/long-beach-county-census.json
sources.not_stated: Anything about the courts themselves, or about any address the operators did not publish.
